items.title: Frank Capp interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: What was it like working with Joe on that album? ... And that album that we did, “Live at the Century Plaza,” ... Joe just turned around and said to Nat, “B flat.” Nat put it down. And we played.

ctx.x: What was it like working with Joe on that album?

Joe Williams is a sweetheart, and he’s a great singer, and he is so laid back. I mean he’ll come into a gig situation, of course he’s got to feel pretty comfortable with who’s on the stand behind him. But he’ll walk in and he won’t have to rehearse anything you know. He’ll bring his charts maybe, maybe he won’t bring his charts, maybe we’ll just fake stuff. He’s so easy to work with. And that album that we did, “Live at the Century Plaza,” we had recorded maybe three or four tunes other than what’s on the album.…

That’s interesting because that’s one of the parts about jazz I think that some people find so fascinating. Like how did you do that — he just said “B flat” and you played for eleven minutes you know. And that’s the beauty of the music in some respects.
